Article 5

1. The implementation of protection of women, children and families who are victims of violence is a comprehensive prevention system, covering protection against all forms of violence, trafficking of women and children, economic exploitation, sexual exploitation, abuse, neglect and or abandonment in all situations including women and children with disabilities, children of migrant worker families, children in conflict with the law, children in emergency situations and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence.
2. The regional government is obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection against all forms of violence against women and children and their families. .

CHAPTER III

OBJECTIVES

Article 3

The purpose of implementing protection of women and children especially victims of violence is to ensure the protection of women and children, so that they do not become victims of violence and to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their families, both before, during and after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

REGENT OF BLITAR

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BLITAR REGENCY

NUMBER 11 OF 2013

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

REGENT OF BLITAR,

a. that women and children are beings created by God Almighty who possess noble rights and dignity in accordance with their nature as human beings; b. that there are still many women and children who do not fully receive their basic rights, especially women and children who are victims of violence; c. that all forms of acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of Human Rights, therefore women and children who are victims of violence need to receive protection; d. that the protection of women and children, especially victims of violence, is one of the obligations that must be carried out by the Regional Government as one of the efforts to realize community welfare; e. that to realize protection for women and children who are victims of violence in an integrated and sustainable manner, institutional support and legislation are required that can guarantee its implementation in a coordinated and directed manner; Considering::

f. that based on considerations a, b, c, d, and e, it is necessary to immediately establish a Regional Regulation of Blitar Regency concerning the Protection of Women and Children

CHAPTER IV

SCOPE

Article 4

The scope of implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence includes:
a. implementation of protection of women and children, both before, during and after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur;
b. regulation of institutions and mechanisms for implementing protection of women and children, especially victims of violence.

Article 14

1. The community may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities for the implementation of protection of women and children, victims of violence especially for women, children and their families.
2. The community who knows, hears, and sees the occurrence of violence is obliged to provide assistance and protection to victims of violence especially women, children and their families.

CHAPTER X

SANCTION PROVISIONS

Article 19

Any person who deliberately allows violence against women and children to occur and/or does not report the occurrence of violence against women and children, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 8

1. The formulation of policies, program planning, and budgets for prevention and safeguarding services shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. mapping, collection, processing, and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence;
b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;
c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and
d. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
2. The implementation of prevention and safeguarding of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. implementation of programs and activities contained in the SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting on policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children.
3. The mechanism for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in the Regent Regulation.
4. The formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of safeguarding for women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD responsible for Regional Development Planning.
5. Prevention and safeguarding efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims shall be implemented by:
a. forming a network in violence prevention efforts;
b. conducting coordination, integration, and synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders;
c. establishing a violence prevention system, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on violence prevention against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

Article 6

1. Prevention services are all forms of services provided to the general public, especially women and children, in legal, social, cultural, and economic aspects, which have an impact on increasing knowledge, skills, and awareness so that they do not become victims or perpetrators of violence.
2. Safeguarding services are all forms of services provided to the community, especially women and children who are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as that of their families. The services provided include legal, social, cultural, and economic services that have an impact on increasing knowledge, skills, and awareness so that they do not become victims or perpetrators of violence.
3. Handling services include all forms of at least minimum services, including legal, medical, psychosocial, rehabilitation, and social reintegration services provided to women and children who are victims of physical, psychological, sexual violence, trafficking in women and children, neglect, and exploitation.
4. The procedures, mechanisms, and service standards for prevention, safeguarding, and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2), and (3), shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 7

1. The implementation of protection, prevention, safeguarding, and handling of women and children, especially victims of violence, is carried out in an integrated manner, covering legal, medical, medicolegal, and psychosocial aspects, by the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) or another name that has the same role and function as P2TP2A.
2. The P2TP2A institution and/or other similar names shall be established by Regent Decree.
3. The implementation of P2TP2A services and/or other names shall be carried out in accordance with the Minimum Service Standards (SPM) and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) in accordance with statutory provisions.

CHAPTER XI

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 23

At the time this Regional Regulation is stipulated and promulgated, all provisions relating to the protection of women and children, especially victims of violence, shall remain in force insofar as they are not contrary to this Regional Regulation.

Article 15

The Business Sector may play a role in implementing obligations and responsibilities towards the provision of protection for victims of violence, especially for women, children and their families.

Article 10

Regional Government, community, and business sector are obliged and responsible for the implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence and their families.

CHAPTER VII

FINANCING

Article 16

1. Financing for the provision of protection for women and children, prevention, safeguarding and handling of victims of violence especially women and children, shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of the Regency, through the SKPD responsible for women and child protection affairs.
2. Budget management for the provision of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted with the principles of fairness, efficiency, transparency and accountability.

CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN, ESPECIALLY VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 20

1. Any person who discloses the whereabouts of a victim of violence who is being placed in a confidential location, shall be threatened with confinement for a maximum of 3 (three) months or a fine of a maximum of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).
2. In the event that the act as referred to in paragraph (1) is committed by an official appointed to provide protection, shall be threatened with confinement for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of a maximum of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

Article 21

Organizers or managers of P2TPA and/or Safe Houses who are proven to collect fees from victims of violence shall be threatened with confinement for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of a maximum of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

CHAPTER VIII

EVALUATION, REPORTING AND ACCOUNTABILITY

Article 17

1. Evaluation, reporting and accountability by P2TP2A or other similar names as the institution providing protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted periodically to the Regent.
2. The mechanism for evaluation, reporting and supervision of the provision of protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, shall be regulated by Regent's Decree.

Part Five

Forms and Mechanisms of Services for Handling Victims of Violence

Article 13

In coordinating the implementation of protection of victims of violence especially for women, children and their families, the Regional Government appoints the Regional Government Work Unit (SKPD) responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as coordinator.

Part Four

Forms and Mechanisms of Prevention and Safeguarding Services

Part One

General

1.4.text:
Article 6

1. Prevention services are all forms of services provided to the general public, especially women and children, in legal, social, cultural, and economic aspects, which have an impact on increasing knowledge, skills, and awareness so that they do not become victims or perpetrators of violence.
2. Safeguarding services are all forms of services provided to the community, especially women and children who are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as that of their families. The services provided include legal, social, cultural, and economic services that have an impact on increasing knowledge, skills, and awareness so that they do not become victims or perpetrators of violence.
3. Handling services include all forms of at least minimum services, including legal, medical, psychosocial, rehabilitation, and social reintegration services provided to women and children who are victims of physical, psychological, sexual violence, trafficking in women and children, neglect, and exploitation.
4. The procedures, mechanisms, and service standards for prevention, safeguarding, and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2), and (3), shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 5

1. The implementation of protection of women, children and families who are victims of violence is a comprehensive prevention system, covering protection against all forms of violence, trafficking of women and children, economic exploitation, sexual exploitation, abuse, neglect and or abandonment in all situations including women and children with disabilities, children of migrant worker families, children in conflict with the law, children in emergency situations and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence.
2. The regional government is obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection against all forms of violence against women and children and their families. .

CHAPTER IV

SCOPE

Article 4

The scope of implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence includes:
a. implementation of protection of women and children, both before, during and after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur;
b. regulation of institutions and mechanisms for implementing protection of women and children, especially victims of violence.

CHAPTER III

OBJECTIVES

Article 3

The purpose of implementing protection of women and children especially victims of violence is to ensure the protection of women and children, so that they do not become victims of violence and to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their families, both before, during and after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER XI

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 23

At the time this Regional Regulation is stipulated and promulgated, all provisions relating to the protection of women and children, especially victims of violence, shall remain in force insofar as they are not contrary to this Regional Regulation.

Article 7

1. The implementation of protection, prevention, safeguarding, and handling of women and children, especially victims of violence, is carried out in an integrated manner, covering legal, medical, medicolegal, and psychosocial aspects, by the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) or another name that has the same role and function as P2TP2A.
2. The P2TP2A institution and/or other similar names shall be established by Regent Decree.
3. The implementation of P2TP2A services and/or other names shall be carried out in accordance with the Minimum Service Standards (SPM) and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) in accordance with statutory provisions.

Article 8

1. The formulation of policies, program planning, and budgets for prevention and safeguarding services shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. mapping, collection, processing, and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence;
b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;
c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and
d. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
2. The implementation of prevention and safeguarding of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. implementation of programs and activities contained in the SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting on policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children.
3. The mechanism for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in the Regent Regulation.
4. The formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of safeguarding for women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD responsible for Regional Development Planning.
5. Prevention and safeguarding efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims shall be implemented by:
a. forming a network in violence prevention efforts;
b. conducting coordination, integration, and synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders;
c. establishing a violence prevention system, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on violence prevention against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

Article 14

1. The community may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities for the implementation of protection of women and children, victims of violence especially for women, children and their families.
2. The community who knows, hears, and sees the occurrence of violence is obliged to provide assistance and protection to victims of violence especially women, children and their families.

CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN, ESPECIALLY VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 5

1. The implementation of protection of women, children and families who are victims of violence is a comprehensive prevention system, covering protection against all forms of violence, trafficking of women and children, economic exploitation, sexual exploitation, abuse, neglect and or abandonment in all situations including women and children with disabilities, children of migrant worker families, children in conflict with the law, children in emergency situations and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence.
2. The regional government is obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection against all forms of violence against women and children and their families. .

Article 13

In coordinating the implementation of protection of victims of violence especially for women, children and their families, the Regional Government appoints the Regional Government Work Unit (SKPD) responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as coordinator.

CHAPTER III

OBJECTIVES

Article 3

The purpose of implementing protection of women and children especially victims of violence is to ensure the protection of women and children, so that they do not become victims of violence and to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their families, both before, during and after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 14

1. The community may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities for the implementation of protection of women and children, victims of violence especially for women, children and their families.
2. The community who knows, hears, and sees the occurrence of violence is obliged to provide assistance and protection to victims of violence especially women, children and their families.

CHAPTER VII

FINANCING

Article 16

1. Financing for the provision of protection for women and children, prevention, safeguarding and handling of victims of violence especially women and children, shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of the Regency, through the SKPD responsible for women and child protection affairs.
2. Budget management for the provision of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted with the principles of fairness, efficiency, transparency and accountability.

Article 6

1. Prevention services are all forms of services provided to the general public, especially women and children, in legal, social, cultural, and economic aspects, which have an impact on increasing knowledge, skills, and awareness so that they do not become victims or perpetrators of violence.
2. Safeguarding services are all forms of services provided to the community, especially women and children who are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as that of their families. The services provided include legal, social, cultural, and economic services that have an impact on increasing knowledge, skills, and awareness so that they do not become victims or perpetrators of violence.
3. Handling services include all forms of at least minimum services, including legal, medical, psychosocial, rehabilitation, and social reintegration services provided to women and children who are victims of physical, psychological, sexual violence, trafficking in women and children, neglect, and exploitation.
4. The procedures, mechanisms, and service standards for prevention, safeguarding, and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2), and (3), shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 10

Regional Government, community, and business sector are obliged and responsible for the implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence and their families.

Article 8

1. The formulation of policies, program planning, and budgets for prevention and safeguarding services shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. mapping, collection, processing, and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence;
b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;
c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and
d. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
2. The implementation of prevention and safeguarding of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. implementation of programs and activities contained in the SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting on policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children.
3. The mechanism for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in the Regent Regulation.
4. The formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of safeguarding for women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD responsible for Regional Development Planning.
5. Prevention and safeguarding efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims shall be implemented by:
a. forming a network in violence prevention efforts;
b. conducting coordination, integration, and synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders;
c. establishing a violence prevention system, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on violence prevention against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

d. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
2. The implementation of prevention and safeguarding of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. implementation of programs and activities contained in the SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting on policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children.
3. The mechanism for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in the Regent Regulation.
4. The formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of safeguarding for women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD responsible for Regional Development Planning.
5. Prevention and safeguarding efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims shall be implemented by:
a. forming a network in violence prevention efforts;
b. conducting coordination, integration, and synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders;
c. establishing a violence prevention system, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on violence prevention against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

Part Five

Forms and Mechanisms of Services for Handling Victims of Violence

Article 6

1. Prevention services are all forms of services provided to the general public, especially women and children, in legal, social, cultural, and economic aspects, which have an impact on increasing knowledge, skills, and awareness so that they do not become victims or perpetrators of violence.
2. Safeguarding services are all forms of services provided to the community, especially women and children who are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as that of their families. The services provided include legal, social, cultural, and economic services that have an impact on increasing knowledge, skills, and awareness so that they do not become victims or perpetrators of violence.
3. Handling services include all forms of at least minimum services, including legal, medical, psychosocial, rehabilitation, and social reintegration services provided to women and children who are victims of physical, psychological, sexual violence, trafficking in women and children, neglect, and exploitation.
4. The procedures, mechanisms, and service standards for prevention, safeguarding, and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2), and (3), shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 7

1. The implementation of protection, prevention, safeguarding, and handling of women and children, especially victims of violence, is carried out in an integrated manner, covering legal, medical, medicolegal, and psychosocial aspects, by the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) or another name that has the same role and function as P2TP2A.
2. The P2TP2A institution and/or other similar names shall be established by Regent Decree.
3. The implementation of P2TP2A services and/or other names shall be carried out in accordance with the Minimum Service Standards (SPM) and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) in accordance with statutory provisions.

CHAPTER X

SANCTION PROVISIONS

Article 19

Any person who deliberately allows violence against women and children to occur and/or does not report the occurrence of violence against women and children, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER IV

SCOPE

Article 4

The scope of implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence includes:
a. implementation of protection of women and children, both before, during and after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur;
b. regulation of institutions and mechanisms for implementing protection of women and children, especially victims of violence.

Article 20

1. Any person who discloses the whereabouts of a victim of violence who is being placed in a confidential location, shall be threatened with confinement for a maximum of 3 (three) months or a fine of a maximum of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).
2. In the event that the act as referred to in paragraph (1) is committed by an official appointed to provide protection, shall be threatened with confinement for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of a maximum of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

Article 14

1. The community may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities for the implementation of protection of women and children, victims of violence especially for women, children and their families.
2. The community who knows, hears, and sees the occurrence of violence is obliged to provide assistance and protection to victims of violence especially women, children and their families.

Article 5

1. The implementation of protection of women, children and families who are victims of violence is a comprehensive prevention system, covering protection against all forms of violence, trafficking of women and children, economic exploitation, sexual exploitation, abuse, neglect and or abandonment in all situations including women and children with disabilities, children of migrant worker families, children in conflict with the law, children in emergency situations and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence.
2. The regional government is obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection against all forms of violence against women and children and their families. .

CHAPTER III

OBJECTIVES

Article 3

The purpose of implementing protection of women and children especially victims of violence is to ensure the protection of women and children, so that they do not become victims of violence and to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their families, both before, during and after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

a. mapping, collection, processing, and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence;
b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;
c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and
d. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
2. The implementation of prevention and safeguarding of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. implementation of programs and activities contained in the SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting on policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children.
3. The mechanism for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in the Regent Regulation.

5. Prevention and safeguarding efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims shall be implemented by:
a. forming a network in violence prevention efforts;
b. conducting coordination, integration, and synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders;
c. establishing a violence prevention system, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on violence prevention against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

Article 6

1. Prevention services are all forms of services provided to the general public, especially women and children, in legal, social, cultural, and economic aspects, which have an impact on increasing knowledge, skills, and awareness so that they do not become victims or perpetrators of violence.
2. Safeguarding services are all forms of services provided to the community, especially women and children who are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as that of their families. The services provided include legal, social, cultural, and economic services that have an impact on increasing knowledge, skills, and awareness so that they do not become victims or perpetrators of violence.
3. Handling services include all forms of at least minimum services, including legal, medical, psychosocial, rehabilitation, and social reintegration services provided to women and children who are victims of physical, psychological, sexual violence, trafficking in women and children, neglect, and exploitation.
4. The procedures, mechanisms, and service standards for prevention, safeguarding, and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2), and (3), shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 14

1. The community may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities for the implementation of protection of women and children, victims of violence especially for women, children and their families.
2. The community who knows, hears, and sees the occurrence of violence is obliged to provide assistance and protection to victims of violence especially women, children and their families.

Article 5

1. The implementation of protection of women, children and families who are victims of violence is a comprehensive prevention system, covering protection against all forms of violence, trafficking of women and children, economic exploitation, sexual exploitation, abuse, neglect and or abandonment in all situations including women and children with disabilities, children of migrant worker families, children in conflict with the law, children in emergency situations and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence.
2. The regional government is obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection against all forms of violence against women and children and their families. .

Article 7

1. The implementation of protection, prevention, safeguarding, and handling of women and children, especially victims of violence, is carried out in an integrated manner, covering legal, medical, medicolegal, and psychosocial aspects, by the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) or another name that has the same role and function as P2TP2A.

Article 10

Regional Government, community, and business sector are obliged and responsible for the implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence and their families.

OBJECTIVES

5.6.text:
Article 8

1. The formulation of policies, program planning, and budgets for prevention and safeguarding services shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. mapping, collection, processing, and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence;
b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;
c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and
d. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
2. The implementation of prevention and safeguarding of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. implementation of programs and activities contained in the SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting on policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children.
3. The mechanism for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in the Regent Regulation.
4. The formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of safeguarding for women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD responsible for Regional Development Planning.
5. Prevention and safeguarding efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims shall be implemented by:
a. forming a network in violence prevention efforts;
b. conducting coordination, integration, and synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders;
c. establishing a violence prevention system, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on violence prevention against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

Article 14

1. The community may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities for the implementation of protection of women and children, victims of violence especially for women, children and their families.
2. The community who knows, hears, and sees the occurrence of violence is obliged to provide assistance and protection to victims of violence especially women, children and their families.

Article 6

1. Prevention services are all forms of services provided to the general public, especially women and children, in legal, social, cultural, and economic aspects, which have an impact on increasing knowledge, skills, and awareness so that they do not become victims or perpetrators of violence.
2. Safeguarding services are all forms of services provided to the community, especially women and children who are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as that of their families. The services provided include legal, social, cultural, and economic services that have an impact on increasing knowledge, skills, and awareness so that they do not become victims or perpetrators of violence.
3. Handling services include all forms of at least minimum services, including legal, medical, psychosocial, rehabilitation, and social reintegration services provided to women and children who are victims of physical, psychological, sexual violence, trafficking in women and children, neglect, and exploitation.
4. The procedures, mechanisms, and service standards for prevention, safeguarding, and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2), and (3), shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 5

1. The implementation of protection of women, children and families who are victims of violence is a comprehensive prevention system, covering protection against all forms of violence, trafficking of women and children, economic exploitation, sexual exploitation, abuse, neglect and or abandonment in all situations including women and children with disabilities, children of migrant worker families, children in conflict with the law, children in emergency situations and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence.
2. The regional government is obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection against all forms of violence against women and children and their families. .

Article 20

1. Any person who discloses the whereabouts of a victim of violence who is being placed in a confidential location, shall be threatened with confinement for a maximum of 3 (three) months or a fine of a maximum of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).
2. In the event that the act as referred to in paragraph (1) is committed by an official appointed to provide protection, shall be threatened with confinement for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of a maximum of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

Article 10

Regional Government, community, and business sector are obliged and responsible for the implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence and their families.

Article 15

The Business Sector may play a role in implementing obligations and responsibilities towards the provision of protection for victims of violence, especially for women, children and their families.

Article 8

1. The formulation of policies, program planning, and budgets for prevention and safeguarding services shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. mapping, collection, processing, and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence;
b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;
c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and
d. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
2. The implementation of prevention and safeguarding of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. implementation of programs and activities contained in the SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting on policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children.
3. The mechanism for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in the Regent Regulation.
4. The formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of safeguarding for women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD responsible for Regional Development Planning.
5. Prevention and safeguarding efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims shall be implemented by:
a. forming a network in violence prevention efforts;
b. conducting coordination, integration, and synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders;
c. establishing a violence prevention system, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on violence prevention against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

CHAPTER VIII

EVALUATION, REPORTING AND ACCOUNTABILITY

Article 17

1. Evaluation, reporting and accountability by P2TP2A or other similar names as the institution providing protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted periodically to the Regent.
2. The mechanism for evaluation, reporting and supervision of the provision of protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, shall be regulated by Regent's Decree.

Article 6

1. Prevention services are all forms of services provided to the general public, especially women and children, in legal, social, cultural, and economic aspects, which have an impact on increasing knowledge, skills, and awareness so that they do not become victims or perpetrators of violence.
2. Safeguarding services are all forms of services provided to the community, especially women and children who are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as that of their families. The services provided include legal, social, cultural, and economic services that have an impact on increasing knowledge, skills, and awareness so that they do not become victims or perpetrators of violence.
3. Handling services include all forms of at least minimum services, including legal, medical, psychosocial, rehabilitation, and social reintegration services provided to women and children who are victims of physical, psychological, sexual violence, trafficking in women and children, neglect, and exploitation.
4. The procedures, mechanisms, and service standards for prevention, safeguarding, and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2), and (3), shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

6.3.text:
Article 5

1. The implementation of protection of women, children and families who are victims of violence is a comprehensive prevention system, covering protection against all forms of violence, trafficking of women and children, economic exploitation, sexual exploitation, abuse, neglect and or abandonment in all situations including women and children with disabilities, children of migrant worker families, children in conflict with the law, children in emergency situations and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence.
2. The regional government is obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection against all forms of violence against women and children and their families. .

Article 15

The Business Sector may play a role in implementing obligations and responsibilities towards the provision of protection for victims of violence, especially for women, children and their families.

CHAPTER III

OBJECTIVES

Article 3

The purpose of implementing protection of women and children especially victims of violence is to ensure the protection of women and children, so that they do not become victims of violence and to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their families, both before, during and after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER IV

SCOPE

Article 4

The scope of implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence includes:
a. implementation of protection of women and children, both before, during and after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur;
b. regulation of institutions and mechanisms for implementing protection of women and children, especially victims of violence.

CHAPTER XI

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 23

At the time this Regional Regulation is stipulated and promulgated, all provisions relating to the protection of women and children, especially victims of violence, shall remain in force insofar as they are not contrary to this Regional Regulation.

Article 14

1. The community may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities for the implementation of protection of women and children, victims of violence especially for women, children and their families.
2. The community who knows, hears, and sees the occurrence of violence is obliged to provide assistance and protection to victims of violence especially women, children and their families.

CHAPTER VII

FINANCING

Article 16

1. Financing for the provision of protection for women and children, prevention, safeguarding and handling of victims of violence especially women and children, shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of the Regency, through the SKPD responsible for women and child protection affairs.
2. Budget management for the provision of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted with the principles of fairness, efficiency, transparency and accountability.

Article 7

1. The implementation of protection, prevention, safeguarding, and handling of women and children, especially victims of violence, is carried out in an integrated manner, covering legal, medical, medicolegal, and psychosocial aspects, by the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) or another name that has the same role and function as P2TP2A.
2. The P2TP2A institution and/or other similar names shall be established by Regent Decree.
3. The implementation of P2TP2A services and/or other names shall be carried out in accordance with the Minimum Service Standards (SPM) and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) in accordance with statutory provisions.

Article 10

Regional Government, community, and business sector are obliged and responsible for the implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence and their families.

CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN, ESPECIALLY VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 8

1. The formulation of policies, program planning, and budgets for prevention and safeguarding services shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. mapping, collection, processing, and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence;
b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;
c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and
d. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
2. The implementation of prevention and safeguarding of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. implementation of programs and activities contained in the SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting on policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children.
3. The mechanism for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in the Regent Regulation.
4. The formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of safeguarding for women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD responsible for Regional Development Planning.
5. Prevention and safeguarding efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims shall be implemented by:
a. forming a network in violence prevention efforts;
b. conducting coordination, integration, and synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders;
c. establishing a violence prevention system, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on violence prevention against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

General

Part One

General

Article 13

In coordinating the implementation of protection of victims of violence especially for women, children and their families, the Regional Government appoints the Regional Government Work Unit (SKPD) responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as coordinator.

CHAPTER X

SANCTION PROVISIONS

Article 19

Any person who deliberately allows violence against women and children to occur and/or does not report the occurrence of violence against women and children, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 20

1. Any person who discloses the whereabouts of a victim of violence who is being placed in a confidential location, shall be threatened with confinement for a maximum of 3 (three) months or a fine of a maximum of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).
2. In the event that the act as referred to in paragraph (1) is committed by an official appointed to provide protection, shall be threatened with confinement for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of a maximum of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

Part Four

Forms and Mechanisms of Prevention and Safeguarding Services

6.6.text:
Article 5

1. The implementation of protection of women, children and families who are victims of violence is a comprehensive prevention system, covering protection against all forms of violence, trafficking of women and children, economic exploitation, sexual exploitation, abuse, neglect and or abandonment in all situations including women and children with disabilities, children of migrant worker families, children in conflict with the law, children in emergency situations and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence.
2. The regional government is obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection against all forms of violence against women and children and their families. .

Article 14

1. The community may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities for the implementation of protection of women and children, victims of violence especially for women, children and their families.
2. The community who knows, hears, and sees the occurrence of violence is obliged to provide assistance and protection to victims of violence especially women, children and their families.

Article 10

Regional Government, community, and business sector are obliged and responsible for the implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence and their families.

CHAPTER III

OBJECTIVES

Article 3

The purpose of implementing protection of women and children especially victims of violence is to ensure the protection of women and children, so that they do not become victims of violence and to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their families, both before, during and after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 15

The Business Sector may play a role in implementing obligations and responsibilities towards the provision of protection for victims of violence, especially for women, children and their families.

Article 13

In coordinating the implementation of protection of victims of violence especially for women, children and their families, the Regional Government appoints the Regional Government Work Unit (SKPD) responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as coordinator.

Article 6

1. Prevention services are all forms of services provided to the general public, especially women and children, in legal, social, cultural, and economic aspects, which have an impact on increasing knowledge, skills, and awareness so that they do not become victims or perpetrators of violence.
2. Safeguarding services are all forms of services provided to the community, especially women and children who are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as that of their families. The services provided include legal, social, cultural, and economic services that have an impact on increasing knowledge, skills, and awareness so that they do not become victims or perpetrators of violence.
3. Handling services include all forms of at least minimum services, including legal, medical, psychosocial, rehabilitation, and social reintegration services provided to women and children who are victims of physical, psychological, sexual violence, trafficking in women and children, neglect, and exploitation.
4. The procedures, mechanisms, and service standards for prevention, safeguarding, and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2), and (3), shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER IV

SCOPE

Article 4

The scope of implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence includes:
a. implementation of protection of women and children, both before, during and after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur;
b. regulation of institutions and mechanisms for implementing protection of women and children, especially victims of violence.

Article 7

1. The implementation of protection, prevention, safeguarding, and handling of women and children, especially victims of violence, is carried out in an integrated manner, covering legal, medical, medicolegal, and psychosocial aspects, by the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) or another name that has the same role and function as P2TP2A.
2. The P2TP2A institution and/or other similar names shall be established by Regent Decree.
3. The implementation of P2TP2A services and/or other names shall be carried out in accordance with the Minimum Service Standards (SPM) and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) in accordance with statutory provisions.

CHAPTER XI

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 23

At the time this Regional Regulation is stipulated and promulgated, all provisions relating to the protection of women and children, especially victims of violence, shall remain in force insofar as they are not contrary to this Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN, ESPECIALLY VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

CHAPTER VII

FINANCING

Article 16

1. Financing for the provision of protection for women and children, prevention, safeguarding and handling of victims of violence especially women and children, shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of the Regency, through the SKPD responsible for women and child protection affairs.
2. Budget management for the provision of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted with the principles of fairness, efficiency, transparency and accountability.

Article 8

1. The formulation of policies, program planning, and budgets for prevention and safeguarding services shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. mapping, collection, processing, and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence;
b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;
c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and
d. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
2. The implementation of prevention and safeguarding of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. implementation of programs and activities contained in the SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting on policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children.
3. The mechanism for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in the Regent Regulation.
4. The formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of safeguarding for women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD responsible for Regional Development Planning.
5. Prevention and safeguarding efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims shall be implemented by:
a. forming a network in violence prevention efforts;
b. conducting coordination, integration, and synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders;
c. establishing a violence prevention system, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on violence prevention against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

Article 17

2. The mechanism for evaluation, reporting and supervision of the provision of protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, shall be regulated by Regent's Decree.

CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN, ESPECIALLY VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 6

1. Prevention services are all forms of services provided to the general public, especially women and children, in legal, social, cultural, and economic aspects, which have an impact on increasing knowledge, skills, and awareness so that they do not become victims or perpetrators of violence.
2. Safeguarding services are all forms of services provided to the community, especially women and children who are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as that of their families. The services provided include legal, social, cultural, and economic services that have an impact on increasing knowledge, skills, and awareness so that they do not become victims or perpetrators of violence.
3. Handling services include all forms of at least minimum services, including legal, medical, psychosocial, rehabilitation, and social reintegration services provided to women and children who are victims of physical, psychological, sexual violence, trafficking in women and children, neglect, and exploitation.
4. The procedures, mechanisms, and service standards for prevention, safeguarding, and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2), and (3), shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VII

FINANCING

Article 16

1. Financing for the provision of protection for women and children, prevention, safeguarding and handling of victims of violence especially women and children, shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of the Regency, through the SKPD responsible for women and child protection affairs.
2. Budget management for the provision of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted with the principles of fairness, efficiency, transparency and accountability.

Article 8

1. The formulation of policies, program planning, and budgets for prevention and safeguarding services shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. mapping, collection, processing, and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence;
b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;
c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and
d. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
2. The implementation of prevention and safeguarding of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. implementation of programs and activities contained in the SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting on policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children.
3. The mechanism for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in the Regent Regulation.
4. The formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of safeguarding for women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD responsible for Regional Development Planning.
5. Prevention and safeguarding efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims shall be implemented by:
a. forming a network in violence prevention efforts;
b. conducting coordination, integration, and synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders;
c. establishing a violence prevention system, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on violence prevention against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

Article 15

The Business Sector may play a role in implementing obligations and responsibilities towards the provision of protection for victims of violence, especially for women, children and their families.

CHAPTER VIII

EVALUATION, REPORTING AND ACCOUNTABILITY

Article 17

1. Evaluation, reporting and accountability by P2TP2A or other similar names as the institution providing protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted periodically to the Regent.
2. The mechanism for evaluation, reporting and supervision of the provision of protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, shall be regulated by Regent's Decree.

Article 10

Regional Government, community, and business sector are obliged and responsible for the implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence and their families.

Article 20

1. Any person who discloses the whereabouts of a victim of violence who is being placed in a confidential location, shall be threatened with confinement for a maximum of 3 (three) months or a fine of a maximum of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).
2. In the event that the act as referred to in paragraph (1) is committed by an official appointed to provide protection, shall be threatened with confinement for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of a maximum of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

Article 13

In coordinating the implementation of protection of victims of violence especially for women, children and their families, the Regional Government appoints the Regional Government Work Unit (SKPD) responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as coordinator.

CHAPTER III

OBJECTIVES

Article 3

Article 5

The implementation of protection of women, children and families who are victims of violence is a comprehensive prevention system, covering protection against all forms of violence, trafficking of women and children, economic exploitation, sexual exploitation, abuse, neglect and or abandonment in all situations including women and children with disabilities, children of migrant worker families, children in conflict with the law, children in emergency situations and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence.
2. The regional government is obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection against all forms of violence against women and children and their families. .

CHAPTER IV

SCOPE

Article 4

The scope of implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence includes:
a. implementation of protection of women and children, both before, during and after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur;
b. regulation of institutions and mechanisms for implementing protection of women and children, especially victims of violence.

Article 14

1. The community may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities for the implementation of protection of women and children, victims of violence especially for women, children and their families.
2. The community who knows, hears, and sees the occurrence of violence is obliged to provide assistance and protection to victims of violence especially women, children and their families.

Article 8

1. The formulation of policies, program planning, and budgets for prevention and safeguarding services shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. mapping, collection, processing, and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence;
b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;
c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and
d. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
2. The implementation of prevention and safeguarding of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. implementation of programs and activities contained in the SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting on policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children.
3. The mechanism for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in the Regent Regulation.
4. The formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of safeguarding for women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD responsible for Regional Development Planning.
5. Prevention and safeguarding efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims shall be implemented by:
a. forming a network in violence prevention efforts;
b. conducting coordination, integration, and synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders;
c. establishing a violence prevention system, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on violence prevention against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

Article 15

The Business Sector may play a role in implementing obligations and responsibilities towards the provision of protection for victims of violence, especially for women, children and their families.

Article 10

Regional Government, community, and business sector are obliged and responsible for the implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence and their families.

CHAPTER VII

FINANCING

Article 16

1. Financing for the provision of protection for women and children, prevention, safeguarding and handling of victims of violence especially women and children, shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of the Regency, through the SKPD responsible for women and child protection affairs.
2. Budget management for the provision of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted with the principles of fairness, efficiency, transparency and accountability.

CHAPTER XI

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 23

At the time this Regional Regulation is stipulated and promulgated, all provisions relating to the protection of women and children, especially victims of violence, shall remain in force insofar as they are not contrary to this Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER X

SANCTION PROVISIONS

Article 19

Article 8

1. The formulation of policies, program planning, and budgets for prevention and safeguarding services shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. mapping, collection, processing, and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence;
b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;
c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and
d. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
2. The implementation of prevention and safeguarding of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented with the following mechanisms:
a. implementation of programs and activities contained in the SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting on policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children.
3. The mechanism for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in the Regent Regulation.
4. The formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the implementation of safeguarding for women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD responsible for Regional Development Planning.
5. Prevention and safeguarding efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims shall be implemented by:
a. forming a network in violence prevention efforts;
b. conducting coordination, integration, and synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders;
c. establishing a violence prevention system, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on violence prevention against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

Article 10

Regional Government, community, and business sector are obliged and responsible for the implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence and their families.

CHAPTER VII

FINANCING

Article 16

1. Financing for the provision of protection for women and children, prevention, safeguarding and handling of victims of violence especially women and children, shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of the Regency, through the SKPD responsible for women and child protection affairs.
2. Budget management for the provision of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted with the principles of fairness, efficiency, transparency and accountability.

Article 13

In coordinating the implementation of protection of victims of violence especially for women, children and their families, the Regional Government appoints the Regional Government Work Unit (SKPD) responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as coordinator.

CHAPTER X

SANCTION PROVISIONS

Article 19

Any person who deliberately allows violence against women and children to occur and/or does not report the occurrence of violence against women and children, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 15

The Business Sector may play a role in implementing obligations and responsibilities towards the provision of protection for victims of violence, especially for women, children and their families.

Article 20

1. Any person who discloses the whereabouts of a victim of violence who is being placed in a confidential location, shall be threatened with confinement for a maximum of 3 (three) months or a fine of a maximum of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).
2. In the event that the act as referred to in paragraph (1) is committed by an official appointed to provide protection, shall be threatened with confinement for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of a maximum of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

Article 6

Safeguarding services are all forms of services provided to the community, especially women and children who are vulnerable to becoming victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as that of their families. IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN, ESPECIALLY VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 13

In coordinating the implementation of protection of victims of violence especially for women, children and their families, the Regional Government appoints the Regional Government Work Unit (SKPD) responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as coordinator.

Article 14

1. The community may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities for the implementation of protection of women and children, victims of violence especially for women, children and their families.
2. The community who knows, hears, and sees the occurrence of violence is obliged to provide assistance and protection to victims of violence especially women, children and their families.

CHAPTER XII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 24

All forms of operational regulations for the implementation of this Regional Regulation must be in place no later than 6 months after this Regional Regulation is stipulated and promulgated.

CHAPTER III

OBJECTIVES

Article 3

The purpose of implementing protection of women and children especially victims of violence is to ensure the protection of women and children, so that they do not become victims of violence and to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their families, both before, during and after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
